clue.text: Apparently not having a ripping time?

definitions.text: Apparently not having a ripping time?

parts.words: Apparently not having a ripping time?
parts.note: a ripping time is a splendid one, but read literally it is time spent ripping, so someone who feels wearied to the point of weeping is apparently not enjoying it

explanation.surface: Someone at a party seems not to be having a splendid evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ripping' is old-fashioned British slang for excellent; the cryptic reading takes it as tearing, and tears (weeping) arrive with extreme tedium.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone utterly weary and uninterested, the opposite of having a splendid time.

clue.text: A river, surrounded by ooze, became obscured

indicators.note: the article and the river sit inside the word for ooze, enclosed on both sides

parts.note: to ooze is to bleed or seep out

explanation.surface: A river bank turned to mud, and the water clouded over.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes or a view that are bleary have been dimmed or blurred, so became obscured is the verb sense.

clue.text: Surrey town has reduced control over spectators

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece stands over, above, the second
the word for control is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: to rein is to control, as with a horse
the final letter of the control word is the one that goes when it is reduced
the gate is the number of people paying to watch a sports match

explanation.surface: A town in Surrey keeps a tight rein on its sports crowds.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'over' means the first piece sits above the second. Reigate is a market town in Surrey, a county just south of London; a sports 'gate' is the paying crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Reigate is a town in the English county of Surrey, so the clue's description names it by location.

clue.text: Artist to offer lines on love

parts.note: to donate is to offer or give
L is the abbreviation for line, doubled for lines
love is a score of nil in tennis, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: A painter proposes a few lines about love.
explanation.definitionFit: Donatello was a Renaissance sculptor from Florence, an example of an artist.

clue.text: Speak in florid style? That's not new

indicators.note: the clue says the florid word is to be taken without the abbreviation for new

parts.note: ornate means elaborately decorated, in a florid style

explanation.surface: The question is whether flowery speech is anything but old hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speak in florid style' reads as the whole definition, but only 'Speak' defines; ORNATE loses its N (new) to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to speak formally, often pompously, so it is a kind of speaking.

clue.text: Drug received by tearaway gives personal boost

parts.note: E is short for ecstasy, the drug
got means received
a rip is a reckless or dissolute person, a tearaway

explanation.surface: A young tearaway takes a pill and feels better about himself.
explanation.walkthrough: RIP for a rascal is an old British sense, a shortening of reprobate.
explanation.definitionFit: An ego trip is something done chiefly to feed one's own vanity, a boost to self-esteem.

clue.text: Girl is about to reorder later publication

indicators.note: the clue asks for the pieces to be put into a different arrangement

parts.note: re means about, concerning
Sue is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl is about to change the way a list is arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reorder' tells the solver to put the three pieces in a different sequence from the clue's: the girl comes last, not first.
explanation.definitionFit: A reissue is a book or record brought out again after its first appearance.

clue.text: Deliverywoman more severe? Not if American type

indicators.note: Not tells the solver to leave out the following word from the joined pieces

parts.note: a midwife delivers babies
sterner means more severe

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a midwife is stricter, unless she is from the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not if' removes IF from MIDWIFE STERNER to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from the central northern states of the USA is a kind of American.

clue.text: I head round Rhode Island coming from part of Europe

indicators.note: the word for head goes round the state abbreviation, enclosing it

parts.note: bean is slang for the head
RI is the postal abbreviation for Rhode Island

explanation.surface: Someone travels around a small American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Iberian describes things from the peninsula holding Spain and Portugal.

clue.text: Get rid of a lot of nonsense about half-life

indicators.note: the nonsense word is placed about the half piece, enclosing it

parts.note: bosh is a lot of nonsense, rubbish

indicators.note: half of the word life gives its first two letters

explanation.surface: Someone wants to scrap a load of rubbish about radioactive decay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-life' looks like physics but is split: 'half-' takes LI, the front half of LIFE.
explanation.definitionFit: To abolish something is to do away with it formally.

clue.text: I herald'a toss, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone announces a coin toss.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of I HERALD A TOSS gives the call made at a coin toss, so the whole clue both defines and builds the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the call a person makes on a tossed coin, which is what the clue's speaker announces.

clue.text: Guarantee speech in time of conflict?

parts.note: war is a time of conflict
a rant is a loud impassioned speech

explanation.surface: A rousing speech promises something in wartime.
explanation.definitionFit: A warrant is an assurance or authorisation, so it means guarantee as noun or verb.

clue.text: Article is a regret, setting back part of the world

indicators.note: setting back reverses the order of all the letters gathered

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: A newspaper article expresses regret over losing ground in some region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting back' reverses A IS A RUE as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Eurasia is the combined landmass of Europe and Asia, a region of the globe.

clue.text: Players, bagging fourth of goals, move cautiously

indicators.note: the team word bags, holds inside it, the chosen letter

parts.note: a side is a team of players

indicators.note: fourth of picks the fourth letter of goals

explanation.surface: A team scores and edges forward warily.
explanation.definitionFit: To sidle is to edge along furtively or warily.

clue.text: Line misrepresented Keats and Poe as mere versifiers?

indicators.note: the two poets' names are shown wrongly, their letters jumbled

explanation.surface: A line of verse misquotes two famous poets as mere rhymers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mere' looks like 'only' but means a lake; Wordsworth, Coleridge and Southey lived in the English Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: A mere is a lake, so poets of the mere are the Lake District group of Romantic writers.

clue.text: Deadly snake caught in Girobank, surprisingly

indicators.note: the cricket letter is placed in the rearranged bank name
surprisingly signals the bank name turned into an unexpected arrangement

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A venomous snake is found lurking in a bank branch.
explanation.walkthrough: Girobank was a British bank run through the Post Office; its letters rearranged take in C.
explanation.definitionFit: The king cobra is the world's longest venomous serpent, an Asian killer.

clue.text: About to finish, turning depressed? One's taken to bed

indicators.note: turning reverses the letters of the two words before it

parts.note: re means about
to die is to come to an end, to finish
down means depressed

explanation.surface: Someone almost done in and feeling low retires to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses RE DIE to give EIDER.
explanation.definitionFit: A quilt filled with duck feathers is laid on a bed, so it is something taken there.

clue.text: Screen feature showing where schoolkids accumulate marks?

definitions.meaning: on a computer the main background screen holding icons
pupils scratch and ink their names on the upper surface of a school desk

explanation.definitionFit: On a computer it is the home screen; literally the upper surface of a school bench, scratched by pupils.

clue.text: Mechanical maggot, one swallowed by huge old bird

indicators.note: the maggot and the numeral go inside the bird's name

parts.note: the roc is a giant bird of legend
a bot is the larva of the botfly, a maggot
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A giant bird of legend gulps down a grub.
explanation.definitionFit: Something automated, like a machine, behaves in a mechanical way.

clue.text: Tree with fewer leaves? Not at first

indicators.note: the first letter of the bare word is to be left off

parts.note: a tree with fewer leaves is balder, more bare

explanation.surface: A tree is looking sparser in autumn, except at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: The alder is a tree of the birch family growing by water.

clue.text: Article, fashionable, one from The Oaks racecourse

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
in means fashionable
an oak is one example of a tree

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about a classic flat race.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oaks is a famous English horse race, which steers the solver away from trees. Aintree is the Liverpool course of the Grand National.
explanation.definitionFit: Aintree, near Liverpool, is the course where the Grand National steeplechase is run.

clue.text: Daughter is wrong to twist

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: A daughter is wrong to twist the facts.
explanation.definitionFit: To distort is to bend out of shape or misrepresent.

clue.text: Be very taken aback when bitten by horse in place of oats?

indicators.note: the reversed pieces sit inside the horse word, held in its teeth

parts.note: a nag is a horse

indicators.note: taken aback means turned backwards

parts.note: so means very

explanation.surface: A horse bites someone who is startled at feeding time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' turns BE SO into OSEB, which NAG holds.
explanation.definitionFit: A bag of feed hung round a horse's head holds its oats.

clue.text: Girl's name not recorded in marriage venue

indicators.note: the abbreviation for name is left out of the place name

parts.note: Gretna Green in Scotland was famous for runaway weddings

explanation.surface: A girl's name was left off the register at a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: Gretna Green, just over the Scottish border, was where eloping English couples married; GRETNA drops N.
explanation.definitionFit: Greta is a female forename, like Greta Garbo.

clue.text: Article carried by players going to a card-game

indicators.note: the article is carried inside the word for players

parts.note: the cast are the actors in a play
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece accompanies actors heading for a card table.
explanation.definitionFit: Canasta is a rummy-type game played with two packs of cards.

clue.text: Change name of one in scurrilous letter

indicators.note: the numeral is put in the jumbled letters
scurrilous, coarse and abusive, signals the word letter mangled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone appears in an abusive letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To retitle something is to give it a new name.

clue.text: Noisy bird in pub immediately left

parts.note: a bar is a pub
now means immediately

explanation.surface: A loud bird in a pub promptly departs.
explanation.definitionFit: This pale owl is known for its eerie screech rather than a hoot.

clue.text: Spy -fellow linked to various pleas about espionage group

indicators.note: the jumbled pleas go about the agency, enclosing it
various signals the letters of pleas in a different form

parts.note: the CIA is the US intelligence agency
a gent is a fellow

explanation.surface: A man in intelligence makes assorted appeals to a spy agency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' marks the anagram of the clue word pleas, which goes round the American agency; 'Spy' alone defines, and 'linked to' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret operative, as in the FBI, is a spy or field agent.
